ℹ️
Modular Architecture

Trstprep uses a modular structure with feature-based organization. The backend has migrated to a modules-based architecture with dedicated routes, services, and helpers per feature. Models are organized by domain (user, exam, test, question, etc.).

📁 Root Directory

File/Directory Description
package.json Root package.json for monorepo (turbo)
package-lock.json Node dependencies lock file
turbo.json Turborepo configuration
turbo_dry.json Turbo dry-run output (debug file)
deploy.sh Deployment script
README.md Project documentation
.gitignore Git ignore rules
apps/ Application packages (backend, frontend, landing)
packages/ Shared packages (config, ui, utils)
scripts/ Build/dev scripts
dev-tools/ Development utility scripts
docs/ Documentation files

🗄️ Database Schema

ℹ️
Dual Database Architecture

The application uses a dual approach: MongoDB with Mongoose for complex documents and PostgreSQL via Supabase with a helper layer providing MongoDB-like API. All tables support soft delete via is_active flag and have created_at/updated_at timestamps.

📊 Database Statistics

24
Data Models
16
MongoDB Models
8
PostgreSQL Models
7
Repositories
🗃️ Database Models by Domain ▼
Domain Models Storage
User User PostgreSQL
Exam Exam, ExamCategory, ExamSubCategory, ExamYearlyData, ExamUpdate, Stage PostgreSQL
Test Test, TestCategory, TestSeries, LiveTest, Leaderboard MongoDB
Question Question, Passage MongoDB
Attempt Result, SectionAttempt, Enrollment MongoDB
Syllabus Subject, Chapter, Topic MongoDB/PostgreSQL
Subscription SubscriptionPlan, Coupon MongoDB
Content StudyMaterial, Video, CurrentAffair, Notification MongoDB/PostgreSQL
👥 User & Authentication Tables ▼
Table Model File Storage Key Fields Relationships
users user/User.js PostgreSQL id, name, email, password, role, is_pro_user, referral_code → results, enrollments, notifications, bookmarks
notifications Notification.js MongoDB userId, type, title, message, isRead, priority, actionUrl users → (FK: userId)
enrollments attempt/Enrollment.js MongoDB userId, seriesId, status, progress, completedTests[], paymentId users →, test_series →
📝 Test System Tables ▼
Table Model File Storage Key Fields Relationships
test_series test/TestSeries.js MongoDB slug, title, category, totalTests, price, isPro, difficulty, rating → tests, enrollments
tests test/Test.js MongoDB seriesId, title, examType, tier, category, questions, duration, marks, isLive test_series →, → questions, results
test_categories test/TestCategory.js PostgreSQL parentId, name, level, examCategoryId, stageId Self-referential, exam_categories →
questions question/Question.js MongoDB testId, text{en,hi}, options, correctOption, section, difficulty, passageId tests →, passages →
passages question/Passage.js MongoDB title, content, questions[] → questions
section_attempts attempt/SectionAttempt.js MongoDB attemptId, sectionName, totalQuestions, attempted, correct, wrong, marks test_attempts →
results attempt/Result.js MongoDB userId, testId, seriesId, score, correctCount, rank, percentile, answers[] users →, tests →, test_series →
leaderboards Leaderboard.js MongoDB testId, rankings[{userId,rank,score}], totalParticipants, isPublished tests →
live_tests LiveTest.js MongoDB testId, scheduledAt, duration, registeredUsers[], prizes[], isCompleted tests →, users →
🏛️ Exam Information Tables ▼
Table Model File Storage Key Fields Relationships
exam_categories exam/ExamCategory.js PostgreSQL category_id, label, slug, icon, description → exam_sub_categories, exams
exam_sub_categories exam/ExamSubCategory.js PostgreSQL parent_category_id, name, slug exam_categories →
exams exam/Exam.js PostgreSQL category_id, title, full_name, short_name, slug exam_categories →
exam_yearly_data exam/ExamYearlyData.js PostgreSQL exam_id, year, vacancies, exam_date_start, exam_date_end exams →
exam_updates ExamUpdate.js PostgreSQL exam_id, title, content, update_type, date exams →
stages Stage.js PostgreSQL exam_id, name, order, description exams →
📚 Study Materials Tables ▼

🏗️ Architecture Recommendations for Scaling (50k-500k Users)

⚠️
Storage Risk Warning

MongoDB + PostgreSQL dual storage creates maintenance overhead. Consider pure PostgreSQL for structured data or PostgreSQL + Redis for caching only.

1. Modular Architecture (Implemented)

backend/src/modules/
├── analytics/
├── attempts/ (attempt.routes.js)
├── auth/ (auth.routes.js, auth.service.js)
├── community/
├── exams/ (exam.routes.js, examCategory.routes.js, examInfo.routes.js, examYearly.routes.js)
├── questions/
├── study/
├── subscriptions/
├── tests/ (test.routes.js, test.engine.routes.js, test.helpers.js)
└── users/ (user.routes.js)

2. Domain-Based Model Organization (Implemented)

backend/src/data/models/
├── attempt/ (Enrollment, Result, SectionAttempt)
├── exam/ (Exam, ExamCategory, ExamSubCategory, ExamYearlyData)
├── question/ (Passage, Question)
├── subscription/ (Coupon, SubscriptionPlan)
├── syllabus/ (Chapter, Subject, Topic)
├── test/ (Test, TestCategory, TestSeries)
└── user/ (User)

3. Worker System (Implemented)

backend/src/worker/
├── index.js
└── jobHandlers.js

4. Target Architecture

backend/
├── api/routes/           # Legacy routes (being migrated)
├── modules/              # NEW: Feature modules with routes, services
├── data/ (models, repositories)
├── infrastructure/ (database, storage, queue, websocket)
├── services/ (auth, payments, notifications)
├── shared/ (constants, utils, validators)
└── worker/ (job processing)

Database Technology
